decision: Ratify the proposed Class A GitHub issue-closure allowlist A1–A5 and its rollout, or retain human-reviewed closure authority (#2130)?
whyItMatters: CURRENT STATUS: decided, resolution approved (founder ruling, 2026-11-06); the allowlist is ratified policy and operational rollout is a separate verified step. HISTORICAL (pre-ratification, superseded by the 2026-11-06 ruling below; kept as record, not current status): This is new external-write authority, not an extension inferred from local mirror repairs. Engineering proof does not ratify it. The current mission explicitly keeps this Class C decision open.
evidence: HISTORICAL (pre-ratification, superseded by the 2026-11-06 ruling below; kept as record, not current status): The Oct 21 architecture brief and earlier version of this record claimed founder authorization without a separately verified ruling. That inference is superseded by the current mission: the allowlist remains an unratified proposal. No historical approval is asserted here.

STILL CURRENT (engineering fact, unchanged by the ratification): POLICY.yaml retains the disabled implementation: writesEnabled is false, the proposed rules are enumerated, maxClosuresPerRun is 10, and a5Disabled is empty. Editing the switch alone cannot activate it: runtime also requires this record to be explicitly decided with resolution approved. Decided-but-rejected is not authority.

STILL CURRENT (engineering fact, unchanged by the ratification): Both script entrypoints and the public library executor re-derive proof from the checkout, require a complete fresh census and unchanged item digest, reserve bounded budget, and compare live issue and complete comment history before closing.

STILL CURRENT (engineering fact, unchanged by the ratification): Mock tests cover comment-then-close crash recovery, foreign or unknown marker authors, maintainer objections, multipart preservation, receipt replay, reopened pairs and unrelated issue protection. No live closure pilot or burn-down is authorized by those tests.

HISTORICAL (pre-ratification, superseded by the 2026-11-06 ruling below; kept as record, not current status): Issue #1981 was accidentally closed during the prior verifier session (Oct 22 handover). Keeping or reversing that incident is a separate founder disposition, not resolved here.

Founder rulings batch 1, 2026-11-06, relayed to the Steward owner (Opus) for #2283 (verbatim): "A. Steward keeps debt low. Closing issues is easy to manage--I can always reopen or create a new issue on the fly. But there should be receipts to know the steward owner accountable."

Ruling as applied: Option A ratified: autonomous Steward issue closure strictly under the A1-A5 allowlist with attributable Steward-owner and worker receipts, exact closure proof, before/after state, reopening respected; ambiguous/contested/unsupported cases excluded. Policy approved; operational rollout once independently verified and existing write switches/gates are explicitly satisfied; no protection bypass.
recommended: Option A ratified: autonomous Steward issue closure strictly under the A1-A5 allowlist with attributable Steward-owner and worker receipts, exact closure proof, before/after state, reopening respected; ambiguous/contested/unsupported cases excluded. Policy approved; operational rollout once independently verified and existing write switches/gates are explicitly satisfied; no protection bypass.
alternative: Keep closures human-reviewed; retain deterministic reconciliation as read-only context and batch review proposals.
unblocks: Only a future decided record with the exact affirmative resolution approved plus an explicitly enabled policy can emit and execute Class A closure actions. Neither a green test nor a writesEnabled edit grants that authority.
